cohort: 14 women who experienced pregnancy-related deaths and underwent autopsy at a tertiary care teaching hospital in northeast India between 2006 and 2015, with ages ranging from 18 to 39 years.
finding: Delays in diagnosis, treatment, decision to transfer, transport, and therapy were identified as the main factors contributing to maternal deaths, which were primarily caused by shock and haemorrhage due to uterine atony, cervical tear, and uterine rupture.
